subject: math
title: Maps and Directions: Position Words, Map Reading and Paths
seo_title: Grade 2 Maps and Directions Math Worksheets: Free, with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Describe the relative positions of several objects and the movements needed to get from one object to another
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on maps and directions for the Ontario curriculum: position words like left of, between and above, reading a simple park map, following moves such as 3 squares right and 2 up, describing paths, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Count the squares you move, not the square you start on.
key_sub: On a map, left and right are the left and right of the page, and up means toward the top. Do one move at a time: 3 right, then 2 up.
body_html:
What a map is

A map shows a place from above, like a bird flying over it. Each shape on the map stands for a real thing.

Where is it?

Use position words: next to, between, left of, right of, above, below. On a map, left and right are the left and right of the page. Above means toward the top of the page and below means toward the bottom.

Example

What is just below the fish tank?

Find the fish tank. Look one square down.

Answer: the carpet

Follow moves

Count the squares you move. Do not count the square you start on. Do one move at a time.

Example

How do you describe the path to the flag?

Count the squares up: 1, 2. Then count the squares right: 1, 2, 3.

Answer: 2 up, then 3 right

Which path is shorter?

Count the squares along each path. The path with fewer squares is shorter. A path with more turns is not always longer.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting the start squareCount the moves, not the square you stand on
Mixing up left and rightHold up your hands: the left hand makes an L
Going down instead of upUp is toward the top of the page
Swapping the moves (2 right, 3 up instead of 3 right, 2 up)Do the moves in order, one at a time
Choosing the path that looks shorterCount the squares on each path, then compare

faq.q: What do Grade 2 students learn about maps in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In the Spatial Sense strand, Grade 2 students create and read simple maps of familiar places (E1.4). They describe where objects are and the moves needed to get from one object to another (E1.5).

faq.q: How can I help my child tell left from right?
faq.a: Hold up both hands with the fingers up and thumbs out: the left hand makes an L. Practise with games like “turn left at the mailbox” on a walk.

faq.q: Why does my child get the wrong answer when following moves on a grid?
faq.a: The most common mistake is counting the starting square as 1. Show that a move goes to the next square, so “3 right” means three jumps, not three squares including the start.

faq.q: How can we practise maps at home?
faq.a: Draw a simple map of the bedroom or backyard from above. Hide a toy and give moves like “3 steps forward, then 2 steps to the left”, then let your child give the directions.

sets.title: Position words on a classroom map: left of, right of, between, above and below

items.q: What is between the door and the computers?
items.e: Find the door and the computers. They are in the same row. The coat hooks are in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just to the left of the computers?
items.e: Start at the computers. Look one square to the left. That square has the coat hooks.

items.q: What is between the cubbies and the plants?
items.e: Find the cubbies and the plants. They are in the same column. The bins are in the middle of them.

items.q: What is between the whiteboard and the sink?
items.e: Find the whiteboard and the sink. They are in the same row. The window is in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just below the fish tank?
items.e: Start at the fish tank. Look one square down. That square has the carpet. The books are just above.

items.q: What is just to the left of the sink?
items.e: Start at the sink. Look one square to the left. That square has the window.

items.q: What is just above the teacher’s desk?
items.e: Start at the teacher’s desk. Look one square up. That square has the whiteboard.

items.q: What is just below the sink?
items.e: Start at the sink. Look one square down. That square has the cubbies.

items.q: What is between the sink and the bins?
items.e: Find the sink and the bins. They are in the same column. The cubbies are in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just to the right of the books?
items.e: Start at the books. Look one square to the right. That square has the whiteboard.

items.q: Which of these is not on the map?
items.e: Read every label on the map. There is a fish tank, a sink and computers, but no piano.

items.q: How many things are in the bottom row of the map?
items.e: Look along the bottom row: the door, the coat hooks, the computers and the plants. That is 4 things. One square is empty.

items.q: What is just above the cubbies?
items.e: Start at the cubbies. Look one square up. That square has the sink. The bins are just below.

items.q: What is just to the left of the coat hooks?
items.e: Start at the coat hooks. Look one square to the left. That square has the door. The computers are just to the right. Do not mix up left and right.

items.q: What is in the top left corner of the map?
items.e: Top is the top row. Left is the left side of the page. The books are in the top left corner. The sink is in the top right.

items.q: Which is next to the plants?
items.e: Next to means touching, side by side. The bins are just above the plants. The square to the left of the plants is empty.

items.q: What is in the bottom right corner of the map?
items.e: Bottom is the bottom row. Right is the right side of the page. The plants are in the bottom right corner.

items.q: What is just to the right of the door?
items.e: Start at the door. Look one square to the right. That square has the coat hooks.

items.q: What is between the books and the carpet?
items.e: Find the books and the carpet. They are in the same column. The fish tank is in the middle of them.

items.q: What is just above the door?
items.e: Start at the door. Look one square up. That square has the carpet.

sets.title: Read a map of a park

items.q: Which picture shows the tree from above, like on a map?
items.e: A map shows things from above, like a bird flying over them. Picture D shows the tree from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: This picture shows something from above. What is it?
items.e: You can see a pillow at one end and a blanket. It is a bed seen from above.

items.q: Which of these is not on the park map?
items.e: Read every label. The map has a splash pad, a BBQ and a pond, but no skating rink.

items.q: How many squares is it from the gate, straight up to the parking lot?
items.e: Count each move up: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4 squares. If you count the gate square too, you get 5, which is too many.

items.q: Start at the swings. Go straight to the left. What is the first thing you reach?
items.e: Start at the swings and move to the left, one square at a time. Skip the empty squares. The first place is the pond. The BBQ is at the far end of the row.

items.q: Which of these is closest to the gate?
items.e: Count the squares from the gate. The picnic table is only 2 squares away (1 left and 1 up). The others are further away.

items.q: Which picture shows the car from above, like on a map?
items.e: A map shows things from above, like a bird flying over them. Picture C shows the car from above. Picture A shows it from the side.

items.q: You walk from the slide straight to the splash pad. Which way do you go on the map?
items.e: The splash pad is below the slide, in the same column. So you go down.

items.q: How many squares is it from the BBQ, straight across to the swings?
items.e: Count each move to the right: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. That is 5 squares. Do not count the BBQ square.

items.q: What is in the bottom left corner of the park map?
items.e: Bottom is the bottom row. Left is the left side of the page. The garbage cans are in the bottom left corner.

items.q: Start at the slide. Go straight down. What is the first thing you reach?
items.e: Start at the slide and move down, one square at a time. Skip the empty squares. The first place is the splash pad.

items.q: What is between the BBQ and the swings?
items.e: The BBQ and the swings are in the same row. Look along the row between them. The pond is the only thing there.

items.q: This picture shows something from above. What is it?
items.e: A round shape with a handle on one side. It is a cup of hot chocolate seen from above.

items.q: What is in the top right corner of the park map?
items.e: Top is the top row. Right is the right side of the page. The snack bar is in the top right corner. The washrooms are in the top left.

items.q: Which picture shows the table with 4 chairs from above, like on a map?
items.e: A map shows things from above, like a bird flying over them. Picture A shows the table with 4 chairs from above. Picture B shows it from the side.

items.q: How many places are in the top row of the map?
items.e: The top row has the washrooms, the parking lot and the snack bar. The parking lot takes up 2 squares, but it is 1 place. That is 3 places.

items.q: You walk from the pond straight to the swings. Which way do you go on the map?
items.e: The swings are to the right of the pond, in the same row. So you go right.

items.q: Start at the BBQ. Go straight to the right. What is the first thing you reach?
items.e: Start at the BBQ and move to the right, one square at a time. Skip the empty squares. The first place is the pond. The swings are further along the same row.

items.q: What is between the washrooms and the garbage cans?
items.e: The washrooms and the garbage cans are in the same column. Look along the column between them. The BBQ is the only thing there.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go straight up. What is the first thing you reach?
items.e: Start at the gate and move up, one square at a time. Skip the empty squares. The first place is the pond. The parking lot is further up.

sets.title: Follow moves: 3 squares right, 2 squares up

items.q: Start at the house. Go 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 3 squares right, then 2 squares up, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on A. Counting the house square at each move stops you on B.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 2 squares left, then 3 squares up. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 2 squares left, then 3 squares up, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on D. Counting the house square at each move stops you on A.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 3 squares up. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 3 squares up, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on A. Counting the house square as 1 stops you on B.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 4 squares right, then 2 squares down. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 4 squares right, then 2 squares down, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on B. Counting the house square at each move stops you on A.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 2 squares down. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 2 squares down, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on D. Counting the house square as 1 stops you on A.

items.q: How many squares is it from the water fountain, straight down to the bench?
items.e: Count each move down: 1, 2. That is 2 squares. Do not count the water fountain square.

items.q: How many squares is it from the bike racks, straight up to the portable?
items.e: Count each move up: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4 squares. If you count the bike racks square too, you get 5, which is too many.

items.q: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares up. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the gate. Go 2 squares up. You reach the sandbox. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the garden. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square down. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the garden. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square down. You reach the gate. Do not count the square you start on. Going up instead of down takes you to the sandbox.

items.q: Start at the hopscotch. Go 3 squares up, then 2 squares right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the hopscotch. Go 3 squares up, then 2 squares right. You reach the maple tree. Do not count the square you start on. Counting the start square stops you at the play structure.

items.q: Start at the bike racks. Go 1 square up, then 1 square left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the bike racks. Go 1 square up, then 1 square left. You reach the garden. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the gym. Go 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the gym. Go 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. You reach the bench. Do not count the square you start on. Counting the start square stops you at the play structure.

items.q: Start at the bench. Go 3 squares right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the bench. Go 3 squares right. You reach the garden. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: Start at the sandbox. Go 1 square down, then 1 square right. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the sandbox. Go 1 square down, then 1 square right. You reach the bench. Do not count the square you start on. Going up instead of down takes you to the water fountain.

items.q: Start at the swings. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square up. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the swings. Go 4 squares left, then 1 square up. You reach the water fountain. Do not count the square you start on. Going down instead of up takes you to the bench.

items.q: Start at the portable. Go 2 squares down. What do you reach?
items.e: Start at the portable. Go 2 squares down. You reach the swings. Do not count the square you start on.

items.q: How many squares is it from the sandbox, straight across to the swings?
items.e: Count each move to the right: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. That is 5 squares. Do not count the sandbox square.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 4 squares left. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 4 squares left, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on C. Counting the house square as 1 stops you on A.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 2 squares up, then 3 squares left. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 2 squares up, then 3 squares left, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on C. Counting the house square at each move stops you on A.

items.q: Start at the house. Go 3 squares right. Where do you stop?
items.e: Start at the house. Go 3 squares right, one square at a time. Do not count the house square. You stop on B. Counting the house square as 1 stops you on A.

sets.title: Describe a path from one place to another

items.q: Which moves take you from the gym to the bike racks?
items.e: From the gym, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 2 squares right, then 4 squares down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the star. Which moves does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 4 squares left, then 1 square up. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: How many squares long is the dashed path from the red dot to the flag?
items.e: Count each move along the path: 2 up + 3 right = 5 squares. Do not count the dot’s square.

items.q: Which moves take you from the gate to the water fountain?
items.e: From the gate, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 1 square right, then 3 squares up. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 10 squares. Path B is 8 squares. 8 is less than 10, so path B is shorter. 10 − 8 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 3 + 4 = 7 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the tree. Which moves does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 3 squares down, then 2 squares left. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: Which moves take you from the swings to the hopscotch?
items.e: From the swings, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 3 squares left, then 2 squares down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path A?
items.e: Count each move along path A from the house: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: What is the shortest path from the house to the flag? How many squares long is it?
items.e: Go straight across and straight up, with no going back: 5 across + 3 up = 8 squares.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the flag. Which moves does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 2 squares up, then 3 squares right. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: Which moves take you from the sandbox to the garden?
items.e: From the sandbox, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 4 squares right, then 1 square down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 5 + 3 = 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: Which moves take you from the portable to the bench?
items.e: From the portable, count the squares across, then the squares up or down: 4 squares left, then 3 squares down. Count the moves, not the square you start on.

items.q: Follow the dashed path from the red dot to the house. Which moves does it show?
items.e: Count the squares along the path from the dot: 3 squares right, then 2 squares down. Do not count the dot’s own square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. How many squares long is path B?
items.e: Count each move along path B from the house: 4 + 4 = 8 squares. Do not count the house square.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 7 squares. Path B is 9 squares. 7 is less than 9, so path A is shorter. 9 − 7 = 2.

items.q: There are two paths from the house to the flag. Which path is shorter, and by how much?
items.e: Path A is 8 squares. Path B is 8 squares. They are the same length, even though path A has more turns.

sets.title: Word problems: field trips and neighbourhood maps

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. How many blocks is it from the store, straight across to the mailbox?
items.e: Count each move to the right: 1, 2, 3, 4. That is 4 blocks. Do not count the store square.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Leah walks from the park to the pool. Then she walks from the pool to the bakery. How many blocks does she walk in all?
items.e: Park to pool: 1 right + 1 down = 2 blocks. Pool to bakery: 1 right + 1 down = 2 blocks. 2 + 2 = 4 blocks.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Owen walks from the store straight to the mailbox. What does he pass on the way?
items.e: The store and the mailbox are in the same row. The pool is the only place between them.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Mei leaves the washrooms. She goes 2 squares down, then 2 squares right. What does she reach?
items.e: From the washrooms go down 2 squares to the BBQ, then right 2 squares to the pond. Counting the start square each time stops you at the maple tree.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Owen rides his bike from his home 3 blocks right, then 2 blocks up. Where is he now?
items.e: Start at home. Go 3 blocks right, then 2 blocks up. You reach the school. Do not count the block you start on.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Nathan eats lunch at the picnic table. Then he goes to the slide. Which moves take him there?
items.e: From the picnic table, count 3 squares right, then 2 squares up. That is the slide.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Each square on the map is 10 big steps. Ava walks from the gate straight to the splash pad. How many big steps is that?
items.e: The splash pad is 2 squares right of the gate. 2 squares is 10 + 10 = 20 big steps. Counting the gate square too gives 30, which is too many.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Lucas goes from the gate to the swings: 3 right, then 2 up. Emma goes 2 up, then 3 right. Who walks farther?
items.e: Lucas walks 3 + 2 = 5 squares. Emma walks 2 + 3 = 5 squares. They walk the same: 5 squares each.

items.q: Maya draws a map of her bedroom. The desk is to the left of the bed. The door is below the desk. Which map is right?
items.e: Left is the left side of the page. Below means just under. The desk is just left of the bed and the door is just under the desk. That is map B.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Owen wants to go from his home to the library. Which moves take him there?
items.e: From home, count 2 blocks right, then 3 blocks up. That is the library.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Jayden walks from the fire hall 3 blocks down. Where is he now?
items.e: Start at the fire hall. Go 3 blocks down. You reach the bus stop. Do not count the block you start on.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Chloe walks from the library 3 blocks down. Where is she now?
items.e: Start at the library. Go 3 blocks down. You reach the bakery. Do not count the block you start on.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Aiden walks from the gate 2 squares up. What does he reach?
items.e: From the gate, count the moves up: 1 (an empty square), 2 (the pond). Do not count the gate square.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Owen walks from his home 2 blocks up. Where is he now?
items.e: Start at home. Go 2 blocks up. You reach the park. Do not count the block you start on.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Noah walks from the bus stop 1 block up, then 1 block left. Where is he now?
items.e: Start at the bus stop. Go 1 block up, then 1 block left. You reach the mailbox. Do not count the block you start on.

items.q: Lucas draws a map of his backyard. The tree is above the bench. The ball is to the right of the bench. Which map is right?
items.e: Above means just over it, toward the top of the page. Right is the right side of the page. The tree is over the bench and the ball is just right of it. That is map A.

items.q: This is a map of Owen’s neighbourhood. Each square is 1 block. Amira walks from the bakery 2 blocks left, then 2 blocks up. Where is she now?
items.e: Start at the bakery. Go 2 blocks left, then 2 blocks up. You reach the park. Mixing up left and right takes you to the school.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Priya is at the slide. Next she wants a turn on the swings. Which moves take her there?
items.e: The swings are 1 square right of the slide and 1 square down. Mixing up left and right, or up and down, sends her the wrong way.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Benjamin helps at the BBQ. Then he walks 3 squares right and 1 square down. Where is he?
items.e: From the BBQ go right 3 squares, then down 1 square. That is the sandbox. Counting the BBQ square as 1 stops you at the pond.

items.q: The Grade 2 class goes on a field trip to the park. Arjun walks 3 squares right from the BBQ, then 3 squares left. Where is he now?
items.e: 3 right, then 3 left takes him back to where he started: the BBQ.
